sections.title: Climate
sections.filled: Across the surrounding basin of about 3,826 km², rainfall averages about 189 mm a year, strongly concentrated, with August the wettest month. Temperatures there average 28.6 °C, from 21.5 °C in January to 33.8 °C in June. Its aridity index of 0.09 falls in the UNEP arid class. Compared with the five basins around it, its basin receives less precipitation than three and is cooler than three.

sections.title: Water
sections.filled: Timbuktu is about 13 km from the Niger River. Most of the water passing here falls far upstream: the catchment above is 100 times the size of the local basin, and wetter than it. Lakes cover about 0.4% of the basin and wetlands about 37%. The basin drains to the sea about 2,331 km beyond its outlet.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.filled: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Timbuktu itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 3,826 km² that contains it, from global datasets. 3 measures are zero here and so have no percentile: Cropland extent, Karst area, Permafrost extent. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank. River names contain information from OpenStreetMap, available under the ODbL.
